text: dsh-session-bridge 是一个 DSH 工具插件：让 Agent 通过宿主会话服务创建和操作前台会话。插件注册了读取本机 Web GUI 地址、创建会话、发送提示词、读取转录和取消当前回合等工具；提示词可以排队或切换为 steer 模式，读取时可等待回合结束。转录包含消息与工具调用结果，并支持限制返回条数和截断长文本。适合需要让 Agent 在独立前台会话中执行任务并取回结果的场景。会话功能依赖宿主的 sessionController，Web 地址功能依赖 webApp；插件不声明额外 API Key 或外部服务。

dsh-session-bridge is a DSH plugin for agent-operated foreground sessions. Tools create sessions, send prompts, read transcripts and cancel turns; reads can wait for completion. It can also return the local Web GUI URL. It uses host services and declares no extra API keys or external services.
我想让 Agent 新建一个独立的 DSH 前台会话来跑任务。
能不能把提示词发给另一个会话，再把它的回复和工具结果读回来？
想让 Agent 获取本机 DSH Web 界面的访问地址。
dsh-session-bridge 的功能「前台会话操作」：Agent 可创建会话、发送提示词、读取转录并取消当前回合。分别调用对应工具，提示词支持排队或 steer；读取可等待回合完成并返回消息与工具结果。
dsh-session-bridge 的功能「获取 Web 地址」：dsh_web_url 返回本机 GUI 地址，默认遮盖 token；includeToken=true 且权限为 danger-full-access 才返回完整地址。
dsh-session-bridge 使用前须知：默认会遮盖启动 token；只有 includeToken=true 且权限档为 danger-full-access 时，才返回完整地址。（见 index.js:234-267）

dsh-session-bridge README · dsh-session-bridge：Let a [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) agent open
**foreground** sessions, drive them, and read the result back — and hand out the
authenticated URL of the local web app.

dsh-session-bridge README · Why：The Host already has everything needed: `ctx.sessionController` can create, prompt,
inspect and cancel a session, and `ctx.connection.authenticatedUrl()` returns the
web app URL carrying a launch token. None of it is reachable from a model tool.

Without this plugin, an agent that wants to verify something in a real foreground
session has to:

dsh-session-bridge README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh_web_url` | The local web GUI URL. Masks the launch token by default; pass `includeToken: true` to get a browser-usable URL (requires the `danger-full-access` preset). |
| `dsh_session_create` | Create a foreground session. Returns its id. |
| `dsh_session_prompt` | Send a prompt to a session (`queue` or `steer`). |
| `dsh_session_read` | Read a session's transcript. `waitMs` waits for the current turn to finish. |
| `dsh_session_cancel` | Cancel a session's running turn. |

dsh-session-bridge README · Token handling in `dsh_web_url`：The launch token minted by `connection.authenticatedUrl()` is a live credential:
any browser that opens the URL gets an authenticated session. A tool result also
lands in the conversation transcript, and from there into logs, exports and any
copy of the chat.

dsh-session-bridge README · Token handling in `dsh_web_url`：So the default is `maskToken`: the tool returns `origin` plus a URL whose token is
reduced to its first and last four characters. Pass `includeToken: true` only when
something actually needs to open a browser, and do not persist or paste the result.

dsh-session-bridge README · Token handling in `dsh_web_url`：**`includeToken: true` is gated on the caller's permission preset.** The tool asks
the `permissionPresets` service for the calling session's preset
(`current(session)`) and resolves it to `{ sandbox, approval }`. The plain token is
only handed out when `sandbox === "danger-full-access"`; every other preset gets
`insufficient-permission` plus the masked URL instead.

dsh-session-bridge README · Token handling in `dsh_web_url`：The gate fails closed. If `permissionPresets` is missing (older or headless
deployments), if `current()` returns `custom` that `resolve()` cannot handle, if
either call throws, or if `execution.agent.session` is unavailable, the answer is
"no token" — never "allow".

dsh-session-bridge README · Tests：```sh
npm test        # node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

`lib/format.js` holds the pure functions (`maskToken`, `clip`, `reasonLabel`,
`transcribe`, `waitForTurn`); it imports nothing from the Host, so the suite runs
on plain Node 20 with no dependencies. `test/web-url.test.mjs` wires a fake `ctx`
through `apply()` to cover the permission gate, including all the fail-closed
paths.

dsh-session-bridge README · Foreground vs delegated：This is the part that matters. A **foreground** session is a root agent: it has
the `userQuestions` service, so a plugin that needs human consent can actually
ask. A **delegated** task (a subagent, a workflow agent) does not, and gets:

```
APP_APPROVAL_UNAVAILABLE: Application approval is unavailable in delegated tasks; ask the main task to perform this operation
```

dsh-session-bridge README · Foreground vs delegated：So plugins like [dsh-cua-macos](https://github.com/elfgzp/dsh-cua-macos) can only
be exercised end to end from a foreground session — which is exactly what these
tools create.

dsh-session-bridge README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:elfgzp/dsh-session-bridge
```

Restart DSH afterwards. The plugin has no dependencies.

dsh-session-bridge README · Example：```
你手上有一个只能在前台会话里验证的功能。请：
1. 用 dsh_session_create 建一个会话
2. 用 dsh_session_prompt 让它做那件事
3. 用 dsh_session_read（waitMs=120000）把结果读回来

dsh-session-bridge README · Notes：- `dsh_session_read` truncates long text and returns at most `maxMessages`
  messages (default 40). Read a long session in pieces.
- The transcript includes tool calls and their results, so a session that used
  other tools is still auditable from here.
- `dsh_web_url` needs the `webApp` service; a headless deployment has none and
  the tool says so instead of failing.
